primitive.relation: the disjoint union of two graphs on the sum carrier, each summand keeping its own adjacency and nothing across. Simple graphs: Chromatic X66 x66_disjoint_union_rel/x66_disjoint_union are upstream GraphTheory join_rel/sjoin (despite its name the disjoint union), the relation by conversion and the graph pointwise and by the identity isomorphism; the two constructor proofs are related through the graphs they build (eq_diso), never by proof-field equality. Digraphs: Digraph X2 x2_disjoint_union/x2_disjoint_union_rel are Digraph.constructions.digraph_sum digraph_sum/digraph_sum_rel over the existing Finite/HasArc core (no proof fields): the carrier, the relation, every arc and the packaged diGraphType convert. Loops and asymmetric arcs of a summand are kept and either summand may be empty; a join (heroes.djoin, X122 x122_dijoin) is not this construction.

simple-graph-sum.note: upstream join_rel/sjoin on G + H: the relation by conversion, the graph pointwise and by the identity isomorphism; the two opaque constructor proofs frozen with their scripts and related through eq_diso

directed-sum.note: Digraph.constructions.digraph_sum on D1 + D2 with Finite.on and HasArc.Build: the alias, the relation, the arcs and the packaged diGraphType convert; loops, asymmetric arcs and empty summands kept

distinct_variants.Digraph.conjectures.heroes.djoin: domination join H1 => H2: the same sum carrier with every arc from the left summand to the right one added; a join, not the disjoint union
distinct_variants.Digraph.conjectures.X122.x122_dijoin: dijoin L -> R: the same sum carrier with every left-to-right arc added and none back; a join, not the disjoint union
